html:
Melbourne is the capital of Victoria in southeast Australia, at the head of Port Phillip Bay on the Yarra River. British settlers founded it in 1835 on the country of the Wurundjeri and Bunurong peoples, who call the place Naarm.

Settlers came across Bass Strait from Van Diemen's Land (Tasmania). One of them, John Batman, claimed to buy land from Wurundjeri elders in a "treaty" that the governor soon declared void. Sheep runs spread fast across the region, onto the lands of peoples such as the Gulidjan.

The gold rush from 1851 made it, within a few decades, one of the richest cities in the world, "Marvellous Melbourne" of the 1880s. It became the capital of the new colony of Victoria in 1851. Its building workers won the eight-hour day in 1856, and its football clubs wrote the first rules of Australian rules football in 1859.

When the colonies federated in 1901, Melbourne was the seat of the federal parliament until Canberra took over in 1927. It hosted the 1956 Olympics, the first held in the Southern Hemisphere. After 1945 migrants from southern Europe, and later from Asia, made it one of the most mixed cities in the world.
